question: A city has spent €400m of a planned €1bn tunnel. New figures show it will never repay its cost. What should decide whether to continue?
options: Only the remaining €600m against the benefit
answer: The €400m is gone whichever way you choose, so it cannot favour either. The only live question is whether the remaining €600m buys more than €600m of anything else. Counting the spent money is how projects that everyone knows are failing get finished.
move: The money already spent has no vote.
trap: The spent money feels like it would be wasted by stopping.
reference: Arkes & Blumer, The psychology of sunk cost, Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 1985
